title: SUNDAY STORMS
full_story:
National Weather Service Survey Team determined that the tornado that tracked north of Mt. Vernon near Dix and Texico was an EF-3 with maximum winds of 140 miles per hour.  The track was 14 miles long as it continued into western Wayne County.

According to Jefferson County Sheriff Jeff Bullard the two residents that passed away in Sunday night’s tornado were 83-year-old Delores B. Shelton of North Ranch Lane in Mt. Vernon, and 62-year-old Sarita L. Kimble of East July Road in Mt. Vernon, both were in single wide trailers.  The body of one of the victims was found in a debris field outside her mobile home.  The Sheriff and his staff send their condolences to the families.

Cleanup and recovery efforts are currently underway, with volunteer groups including the Southern Baptist Disaster Relief working alongside government agencies to assist residents in the impacted areas.  Currently there are multiple Damage Assessment Teams actively working to survey the impacted area.

Officials advise that individuals without emergency business should continue to avoid the northeastern section of Jefferson County to allow responders and cleanup crews to work safely and efficiently.

The initial survey results are also back on the tornado east of Kinmundy in the Meachum Road area.  The National Weather Service at St. Louis rated it an EF-1 tornado with multi-vortex and a top wind speed of 107 miles per hour.  The path was 2.1 miles long with a maximum width of 190 yards.

The tornado that struck Effingham County on Wednesday night was an EF-3, with estimated peak winds of 150 miles per hour.  Originating in Beecher City within Effingham County, the tornado first touched down along East State Highway 33.  Upon reaching the northern outskirts of rural Effingham, the tornado intensified to EF-3 status as it traveled along East 1800th Avenue.  During this stage, the storm produced peak wind speeds estimated at 145 mph, leading to severe tree damage and the total destruction of one single-family home, which suffered a complete exterior wall collapses.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
Illinois farmers are making quick work of wheat harvest.  USDA’s latest crop progress and condition report showed 41% of the state’s wheat was harvested, up 21 points from the week prior. Harvest pace is well ahead of the same time last year (15%) and the five-year average (32%).  Corn and soybeans are also progressing at or above average pace, with 1% of corn silking and 3% of soybeans blooming.

There were 2.6 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending June 21st.  Statewide, the average temperature was 68.1 degrees, 5 degrees below normal.  Precipitation averaged 1.19 inches, 0.1 inches above normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated at 2% very short, 5% short, 50% adequate, and 43% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 3% very short, 8% short, 61% adequate, and 28% surplus.

Corn emerged reached 96%, compared to the 5-year average of 97%.  Corn silking reached 1%, equal to the 5-year average.  Corn condition was rated 2% very poor, 7% poor, 31% fair, 46% good, 14% excellent.

Soybeans emerged reached 93%, compared to the 5-year average of 92%.  Soybeans blooming reached 3%, compared to the 5-year average of 2%.  Soybeans condition was rated 2% very poor, 7% poor, 33% fair, 44% good, and 14% excellent.

Winter Wheat harvested is at 41% compared to the 5 year average of 32%.  Winter wheat condition was rated 1% very poor, 4% poor, 20% fair, 60% good, and 15% excellent.

title: CHANGE OF VENUE REQUESTED
full_story:
Citing extensive media coverage about former White County jailer Darren Hays’ alleged sexual contact with murder suspect Megan Valentine, her defense attorney has asked the court that her trial be moved out of Edwards County.

Valentine’s attorney, Jessica Koester alleges that “Not only has the media extensively covered the allegations and court proceedings, but the media has also reported extensively on the charges of unlawful sexual conduct.  In referencing the comments posted about various articles about the allegations in the Hays-Valentine matter, Koester writes, “These comments clearly demonstrate a complete lack of impartiality of the potential jury pool in this jurisdiction.

Megan Valentine, 46, remains in the Wayne County jail awaiting trial for the November 5, 2024 shooting death of her husband, Edwards County Circuit Judge Michael Valentine.  Pending motions in the case, including the motion to move the trial out of Edwards County, will be taken up during another pretrial hearing set for this Thursday.

title: INTRODUCTION TO NURSING
full_story:
Lake Land College is hosting an Introduction to Nursing event for high school students on Tuesday, July 14th from 10 am to 4 pm in Neal Hall room 101.  The event is designed for students interested in the nursing profession to learn about the programs and resources available at Lake Land College as well as the career opportunities available in the field.

During the event, students in attendance will meet with faculty and staff, tour Lake Land’s nursing facilities and develop their skills in a variety of hands-on activities.  They will also enjoy the opportunity to experience and practice realistic patient care in the College’s high-fidelity patient simulation lab.  Additionally, attendees will learn everything they need to know about the nursing program admission process, from financial aid options to tips for the entrance exam.  A free pizza lunch will also be provided for all students in attendance.

Space for the Introduction to Nursing event is limited to the first 30 registrants.  Registration is available online.

The Lake Land College Introduction to Nursing Event is offered with sponsorship support from St. Anthony’s Memorial Hospital and Good Shepard Hospital.

To learn more about the Lake Land College Introduction to Nursing Event, contact Nursing Instructor Nichole Jones at 217-234-5455 or [email protected].

title: OUTLAND AIRPORT SELECTED
full_story:
Mt. Vernon Outland Airport is the Terminus host site for the 2026 Air Race Classic, marking a major milestone for both the airport and Mt. Vernon.  The nationally recognized event will bring pilots, crews, aviation officials, and visitors from across the country to Mt. Vernon, making it the largest aviation event hosted at the airport since the 1973 Blue Angels air show.

The Air Race Classic is a prestigious, all-female piloted cross-country air race that traces its roots to the 1929 Women’s Air Derby.  The modern race challenges teams to fly a multi-day route across the United States, testing accuracy, flight planning, and consistency rather than pure speed.  The race concludes at the designated Terminus city, where pilots are welcomed and celebrated for their achievement.  More information about the race is available at airraceclassic.org.

“Being selected as the Terminus for the Air Race Classic is a tremendous honor for Mt. Vernon Outland Airport,” said Chris Collins, Airport Manager.  “This event puts our airport on a national stage and highlights the professionalism of our facilities and staff.  It’s exciting to host an event of this scale and significance.”

Racers and race officials are expected to begin arriving on Thursday, and will remain in Mt. Vernon through Monday, participating in a variety of planned events, receptions, educational opportunities, and community activities throughout their stay.

“This is truly a community-wide opportunity,” said Sheila Jolly Scrivner, Host City Terminus Chair.  “From aviation enthusiasts to families and local businesses, the Air Race Classic offers something for everyone, and we’re looking forward to showcasing Mt. Vernon’s hospitality and support for women in aviation.”

A public aviation celebration and youth activity day will be held on Saturday, from 9 am to 3 pm at Mt. Vernon Outland Airport.  Activities will include Young Eagle Flights for children, interactive aviation displays, educational opportunities, and additional family-friendly programming designed to inspire the next generation of pilots and aviation professionals.

The Air Race Classic is a nonprofit organization dedicated to encouraging and educating women pilots, increasing public awareness of general aviation, and honoring the legacy of women in aviation through an annual cross-country air race.

title: FCC SENIOR CITIZENS DAY
full_story:
Frontier Community College will host a Senior Citizen’s Day event on Friday, September 25th, in West Hall, rooms 103, 104 and 105.

The event is designed to provide helpful information, resources, and support for senior citizens.  The morning will feature presentations from local professionals on topics including financial estate planning, resiliency, hospital resources, healthy meals, adult education, and tutoring opportunities.

Registration and breakfast will begin at 8 am, followed by opening remarks at 8:30 am from Frontier Community College President Dr. Sharmila Kakac and Lori Noe, Director of Learning Commons.

Luke Harl, Financial Advisor with FNB Financial, will present “Financial Estate Planning for Senior Citizens” from 9 to 9:30.  Following a short break, Dana Taylor, Chief Operating Officer at Fairfield Memorial Hospital, will speak on “Resiliency Through Life Challenges” from 9:45 to 10:05.  Taylor will also share information about specialized resources and services available at Fairfield Memorial Hospital.

Additional sessions will include guided breathing imagery provided by Fairfield Memorial Hospital, “Healthy Snacks – Healthy Meals” with Whitney Buckles of Fairfield Memorial Hospital, and “Adult Education – Tutoring Opportunities” with Sharis Wilson, Director of Literacy and Adult Education Operations.

The event will conclude with door prizes and adjournment from 11:30 to noon.  A tour of Learning Commons in Cox Hall will be offered afterward.  During the tour, attendees can learn more about the accommodations and services available to senior citizens upon request.

Advance registration is required to attend.  To register, call Frontier Community College at 618-842-3711.
